description:
Goal
Close the work by deleting obsolete vocabulary, updating docs/guides, and pinning telemetry that proves the single-spine model.

Required docs
Update outline.md or its successor to use ShapeId/LaneId/CallableId/BoundaryId, not ScalarId or LocalCallableId. Update .agent docs and user-facing guides touched by compiler2 runtime transport. Document: semantic evidence is not representation obligation; RuntimeDemand is pre-spine; Shape is settled once and interned all the way down; ValueId maps to ShapeId outside the spine through TransportPosition; facts are tables; divergence is is_empty(return_ty); published boundary contracts are BoundaryId columns, not shape translations; codegen reprs are seam facts, not shape.

Telemetry signal
Expose a transport-spine construction event with stable counts for shape nodes, Nothing nodes, lane leaves, tuple nodes, callable nodes, BoundaryIds, TransportPosition mappings, direct callable transports, first-class callable materializations, omitted lanes, and codegen seam facts. Tests should assert intent through telemetry where that is less brittle than structure dumps. Counts alone are not enough: at least one assertion must prove producer return and consumer resume share one ShapeId for the same transport fact.

Removal target
Dead TODOs, stale comments saying RuntimeValueLayout is the authority, stale tests asserting RuntimeValueLayout/DeliveredShape/NativeDemandAbi, compatibility switches, old dump sidecars, and any temporary construction affordance. If anything temporary remains, create a follow-up ticket before closing this one.

Checks
cargo test --workspace or the agreed compiler2 matrix; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; rg confirms removed old-world names are absent or only appear in historical notes that explicitly describe the removed model. rg also confirms ScalarId, LocalCallableId-as-spine, boundary ABI as model language, and codegen-derived shape are absent from live docs/tests.
title: Transport spine: delete old vocabulary, update docs, and pin spine telemetry
